decisions.question: SDD pre-flight for nidana.model.6 (full-review): which model implements each task?

options.label: Opus for Tasks 1 to 5, sonnet for Task 6
options.consequence: The replay plumbing, structure rules, binding plans, runner reports and process shell get the most capable model; the verification doc a mid-tier one.

options.label: Sonnet for the pure tasks 3 and 4
options.consequence: Cheaper, but the binding plans and the runner-report reading decide what every later behavior gate reports.

decisions.chosen: Opus for Tasks 1 to 5, sonnet for Task 6
decisions.why: S97's allocation for full-review phases, as in nidana.model.1 and .2.

decisions.question: The pinned Flutter SDK has no engine artifacts on this machine (S118), so a real flutter test cannot run without downloading them. How do nidana.model.6's tests cover the Flutter runner?

options.label: Against the plan's stand-in SDK only; no test starts the real flutter; the real run is Outstanding, deferred to nidana.flutter.2
options.consequence: The runner's selection, command line and report reading are tested deterministically; whether the real flutter tool behaves as its 3.47.7 source says waits for the first Flutter gate.

options.label: Fetch the artifacts (fvm flutter precache)
options.consequence: A real run here, but a network download outside pub.dev, which the stop policy excludes; it is the owner's toolchain step.

decisions.chosen: Against the plan's stand-in SDK only; no test starts the real flutter; the real run is Outstanding, deferred to nidana.flutter.2
decisions.why: The stop policy names a network resource other than pub.dev; the run decides not to need it. The owner action (precache before the nidana.flutter lane) is in the report notes.

decisions.question: nidana.model.6 Task 4's review found that the runner-report reader ignores done.success false, so a case that errors after its own testDone (result success) reads PASS while dart test exits 1. The brief says only that done decides completeness. Fix it?

options.label: Fix: a visible test with any error event counts as failed; a complete report with done false and no counted failure fails; also an unknown result fails and a JSON event glued after raw stdout is salvaged
options.consequence: The reader fails closed on every runner failure it can see; one fix round.

options.label: Keep the brief's counting rule
options.consequence: A behavior gate can pass on a binding whose case failed asynchronously, the shape the bus's stream and timer suites take.

decisions.chosen: Fix: a visible test with any error event counts as failed; a complete report with done false and no counted failure fails; also an unknown result fails and a JSON event glued after raw stdout is salvaged
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 9 makes the tool exit 1 when any fixture fails; reading that as a binding failing when any of its cases fails, a false PASS is a defect whatever the brief's counting rule. Reproduced on real dart test output by the reviewer.

decisions.question: A run in which every case is skipped: PASS or FAIL?

options.label: PASS, with the skip count in the line (the brief's own test)
options.consequence: A conformance suite that skips everything passes visibly; bindings are authored only through hsdd-contract.

options.label: FAIL as no case ran
options.consequence: Departs from the plan's pinned test; a gate could not skip a case deliberately.

decisions.chosen: PASS, with the skip count in the line (the brief's own test)
decisions.why: Plan-mandated and visible in the counts; package:test treats skipped as passing. The final review left it parked and flagged that the owner should know.

decisions.question: nidana.model.6 Task 5 was Approved with shell.dart at 724 lines. Split the behavior runner out now, or leave it?

options.label: Split now in a controller-ruled fix round (runners.dart behind runBehavior; purity_test allows exactly runners, shell, workspace), with lenient dart analyze decoding and the dead branch removed
options.consequence: One extra dispatch and re-review; the verification doc describes the final layout and nidana.model.7 adds file and cli to a 608-line shell.

options.label: Leave it to nidana.model.7
options.consequence: Cheaper now; the verification doc would describe a layout the next phase changes, and the analyze decoding crash stays.

decisions.chosen: Split now in a controller-ruled fix round (runners.dart behind runBehavior; purity_test allows exactly runners, shell, workspace), with lenient dart analyze decoding and the dead branch removed
decisions.why: The reviewer recommended the split; the plan's file lists predate it and the change is behavior-neutral (replays byte-identical). The lenient decoding fixes a real crash class.

decisions.question: After the one final fix wave, the re-review notes that the doc's decision 4 line says a defect in the suite slug's tree ends the replayed slug's replay with exit 2, when the whole command exits 2 with one error line and no fixture line for any slug. Another fix round?

options.label: Park it: the fix wave is spent; nidana.model.7 narrows the read (routed) and states the corrected behavior; the report flags it for sign-off
options.consequence: The owner signs a sentence that understates the blast radius of one routed defect, with a note saying so.

options.label: A second doc fix round
options.consequence: Exceeds the one-fix-wave cap the run follows.

decisions.chosen: Park it: the fix wave is spent; nidana.model.7 narrows the read (routed) and states the corrected behavior; the report flags it for sign-off
decisions.why: The SDD final review allows one fix wave and one re-review; the residual is wording, not a wrong verdict, and the routed nidana.model.7 change removes the behavior it describes.
